y-m-49-06.title: Four students' proofs: who proved S?
y-m-49-06.topic: Proof methods: contrapositive, contradiction, distinguish converse
y-m-49-06.goal: Choose accepted proof among four; explain what swapped hypothesis/conclusion proves.
y-m-49-06.material:
For natural a,b, S: ‘If ab odd, then a,b both odd.’ Four students claim proof.
가: Try (3,5), product 15 odd, both odd; (7,9) product 63 odd; so S true.
나: Suppose at least one even, call it 2k. Then ab has even factor, so even. Thus odd product means both odd.
다: Suppose both odd: a=2m+1,b=2n+1 (m,n nonnegative integers). Then ab=4mn+2m+2n+1=2(2mn+m+n)+1, odd. So S proved.
라: Suppose ab odd and a even. If a=2k, ab=2kb even, contradicting odd, so a odd. Similarly b odd. 3 5 15 7 9 63 2 2 2 1 2 1 0 4 2 2 1 2 2 1 2 2

y-m-49-06.s.s1.r.a: Few examples can't prove for all natural a,b. Look for general reasoning.
y-m-49-06.s.s1.r.b: This explains why proving contrapositive proves original.
y-m-49-06.s.s1.r.c: Compare its hypothesis and conclusion with S; same order?
y-m-49-06.s.s1.r.d: This points out contradiction proof structure: contradiction to assumption shows assumption wrong.
y-m-49-06.s.s1.explain: 나 proves contrapositive (if at least one even, ab even); 라 uses contradiction. 가 only checks examples; 다 proves converse, swapping hypothesis/conclusion.

y-m-49-06.s.s2.model.1: S assumes ab odd and must show a,b odd; 다 starts assuming both odd. Opposite direction, so not proof.
